tools.name: get_sample_pipeline
tools.description: A fictional pipeline in exactly the shapes the real tools return: an ICP, the signal definitions, pipeline stats and six prospects with their signals, verbatim quotes and drafts. Works without any credential, so an agent can show what Getcleed produces before an account exists. Nothing in it is a re

tools.name: list_prospects
tools.description: Search the saved prospects in the account. Filter by company, industry, job title, country, signal type, minimum number of signals, whether an email address is known, enrichment state, or whether they have been contacted. Ordered by signal count, then most recently saved.

tools.name: get_prospect
tools.description: Everything known about one prospect: role, company, location, language, every detected signal with the verbatim quote from its source and the LinkedIn URL it came from, any existing email or LinkedIn draft, and outreach state.

tools.name: get_pipeline_stats
tools.description: How the pipeline stands: how many prospects, how many carry signals, enrichment state, how many have an email address, how many were contacted, what was added in the last 7 days, the most common signal types, and the remaining plan quota.

tools.name: list_signals
tools.description: The buying signals this account looks for: the predefined ones and the custom ones, each with the definition used to detect it and whether it is enabled. Use the returned type values with list_prospects and find_leads_from_signals.

tools.name: get_icp
tools.description: The active targeting (ICP): target roles, industries, countries, company sizes, relevant keywords and every saved exclusion. This is what find_leads searches for and what scoring filters against. Change it with update_targeting, add_exclusion and remove_exclusion.

tools.name: add_leads_from_urls
tools.description: Save LinkedIn profiles as prospects and enrich them (name, role, company, industry, location, language). Skips anyone already saved. Counts against the import quota.

tools.name: find_leads_from_signals
tools.description: Search recent LinkedIn posts on the topics of this account's own signal definitions, keep only posts a check can prove are on topic, and return the people who wrote, commented on or reacted to them, filtered against the ICP (role, industry, country) and ranked. Nothing is saved: pass the returned ca

tools.name: import_sourced_leads
tools.description: Save candidates returned by find_leads_from_signals. They arrive already enriched and with the signal attached, including the verbatim quote from the post that surfaced them. Counts against the import quota.

tools.name: analyze_prospects
tools.description: Run the signal pipeline on prospects: enrich anyone missing company data, read their recent LinkedIn activity, and detect buying signals. Every signal kept must quote its source verbatim. Counts against the monthly analysis quota. Slow: expect up to a few minutes.

tools.name: draft_email
tools.description: Write a personalised email for a prospect, built from their detected signals, in their language. Saves the draft on the prospect and returns it. Does not send.

tools.name: draft_linkedin_message
tools.description: Write a short LinkedIn connection note for a prospect from their detected signals, in their language. Saves the draft and returns it. Does not send. Drafts follow the house rules (one fact about them, one question, no pitch, under 200 characters) and so must any note passed to send_linkedin_message.

tools.name: send_email
tools.description: Send an email to a prospect from the connected mailbox. This reaches a real person immediately and cannot be undone. Pass the subject and body you want sent, or omit them to send the saved draft. Requires a mailbox connected in getcleed under Integrations.

tools.name: send_linkedin_message
tools.description: Send a LinkedIn connection request with a note to a prospect from the connected LinkedIn account. This reaches a real person immediately and cannot be undone. Pass the note you want sent, or omit it to use the saved draft. Requires LinkedIn connected in getcleed under Integrations.

tools.name: mark_email_sent
tools.description: Record that a prospect was emailed outside getcleed, so reporting and follow-ups stay correct.

tools.name: create_custom_signal
tools.description: Teach the account a new buying signal to look for, described in plain language (for example "people complaining their onboarding takes too long"). Future analyses and sourcing will use it.

tools.name: find_leads
tools.description: Search for a few new people (5 by default, up to 50) matching the account targeting (see get_icp; change it with update_targeting or add_exclusion first if the user wants someone else). Runs in the background for two to five minutes and puts the people found in the review queue: nobody is saved unti

tools.name: get_search_status
tools.description: Whether a find_leads search is running or finished, how many people are waiting in the review queue per search, and the weekly discovery allowance left.

tools.name: list_search_results
tools.description: People found by searches, best fit first. "to_review" is the queue waiting for a decision, "approved" the ones saved as leads, "rejected" the ones marked not a fit (they can be restored with reject_leads undo). Each person has a fit level against the targeting and the reason for it.

tools.name: approve_leads
tools.description: Save people from the review queue as leads (in a list named after their search), and optionally add them to a sequence. Pass ids from one search, or a searchId to approve everyone still waiting in it. If the sequence is running, the first call returns what will be sent and needs confirm: true. Witho

tools.name: reject_leads
tools.description: Mark people in the review queue as not a fit, optionally with the reason. They leave the queue and later searches skip them. With undo: true, brings rejected people back to the queue. When the reason would apply to others too, offer add_exclusion.

tools.name: update_targeting
tools.description: Change who find_leads looks for: target job titles, industries, countries and company sizes. Each field passed replaces that field; fields left out stay as they are. Show the user the current targeting (get_icp) and the change before calling. To exclude people, use add_exclusion instead.

tools.name: add_exclusion
tools.description: Save an exclusion in the account targeting so later searches skip matching people: a job title keyword, an industry, or a company size limit. With candidateId (a result just rejected), matching people still waiting in that same search are removed too. The user can see and remove exclusions with get_

tools.name: remove_exclusion
tools.description: Take one saved exclusion out of the account targeting. Pass it as get_icp lists it under exclusions.

tools.name: list_sequences
tools.description: Every outreach sequence in the account: whether it is running, whether each message is reviewed before sending, its steps in short, and how many leads are in each state.

tools.name: get_sequence
tools.description: One sequence in full: its steps, its sections (the search each group of leads came from, which can be stopped or resumed on its own), and each lead with where they are, what happens next and when.

tools.name: create_sequence
tools.description: Create an outreach sequence. approach "signal": a connection request, then an opener Getcleed writes for each lead from their own signals and two follow-ups (the default, and what the product is for). "simple": four short generic messages. "own": fixed messages you pass, sent to everyone with {{firs

tools.name: add_leads_to_sequence
tools.description: Put saved leads (prospect ids from list_prospects) into a sequence. Leads already in a sequence, dismissed, or who replied are skipped. If the sequence is running, the first call returns what will be sent and needs confirm: true. Without LinkedIn connected and a sending schedule on, the leads wait i

tools.name: start_sequence
tools.description: Start a sequence: its leads are enrolled and steps begin going out on the sending schedule, from the user's own LinkedIn account. The first call returns how many people it reaches and whether messages are reviewed first; it only starts with confirm: true. With section, resumes just that section afte

tools.name: stop_sequence
tools.description: Stop a running sequence: nothing more is sent until it is started again. With section, stops only the leads that came from that search and leaves the rest running. Stopping never unsends anything.

tools.name: list_sequence_messages
tools.description: For each lead in a sequence, the messages still to be sent to them, with the text when it is already written, and the evidence about the lead the text is based on. Use it to show the user what will go out, and before approving a message when review is on (pass the evidenceFingerprint to update_seque

tools.name: update_sequence_lead
tools.description: Act on one lead inside a sequence (enrollmentId from get_sequence or list_sequence_messages). editText rewrites a message not sent yet. status "active" approves the waiting message when review is on (pass the evidenceFingerprint that list_sequence_messages returned with the text the user read) or re

tools.name: list_replies
tools.description: Conversations where a lead answered the outreach and the user has not replied yet, newest first, on LinkedIn and by email. Use the id and channel with get_conversation and send_reply.

tools.name: get_conversation
tools.description: The messages of one conversation with a lead, oldest first, each marked as written by the user or by the lead. Read it before writing a reply.

tools.name: send_reply
tools.description: Send a reply in a conversation, from the user's own LinkedIn account or mailbox. It reaches the lead immediately and cannot be undone: show the user the exact text and get their agreement first. Only conversations started by Getcleed outreach can be answered here.

tools.name: get_account_status
tools.description: Where the account stands: plan and allowances, whether the targeting exists, whether LinkedIn and a mailbox are connected, the sending schedule, and the next steps the product suggests. Steps that need a browser (connecting LinkedIn or a mailbox, billing) come with the link to give the user. Call th

tools.name: update_sending_settings
tools.description: When and how fast sequences send: time zone, days, hours, daily limits, and whether sending is on at all. Fields left out keep their value. Turning it on lets running sequences send: that first call returns the schedule and needs confirm: true, and the first time it also needs the time zone. Needs L

tools.name: set_lead_status
tools.description: Dismiss saved leads (prospect ids from list_prospects): no more outreach goes to them and any sequence they are in is paused for them. "restored" brings dismissed leads back.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "send_email" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "update_targeting" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Change who find_leads looks for: target job titles, industries, countries and company sizes. Each field passed replaces that field; fields left out stay as they…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_prospects, get_prospect, get_pipeline_stats, find_leads_from_signals, find_leads, get_search_status, approve_leads, list_sequences, list_sequence_messages, update_sequence_lead, list_replies, get_conversation · Private data: get_sample_pipeline, mark_email_sent · Public sink: list_prospects, get_prospect, get_pipeline_stats, import_sourced_leads, draft_email, draft_linkedin_message, send_email, send_linkedin_message, mark_email_sent, list_replies, send_reply, update_sending_settings · Destructive: analyze_prospects, add_exclusion, remove_exclusion.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_prospects, get_prospect, get_pipeline_stats, find_leads_from_signals, find_leads, get_search_status, approve_leads, list_sequences, list_sequence_messages, update_sequence_lead, list_replies, get_conversation · Private data: get_sample_pipeline, mark_email_sent · Public sink: list_prospects, get_prospect, get_pipeline_stats, import_sourced_leads, draft_email, draft_linkedin_message, send_email, send_linkedin_message, mark_email_sent, list_replies, send_reply, update_sending_settings · Destructive: analyze_prospects, add_exclusion, remove_exclusion

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "find_leads" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
